items.title: AI Topics Module 2: Education
items.summary: This textbook module examines the intersection of cognitive neuroscience, pedagogy, and artificial intelligence as they converge in the secondary school classroom. Beginning with the theory of mental rigor — the disciplined, sustained exertion of focused cognitive effort as a biological process with measurable neural correlates — the text argues that understanding how the brain learns and understanding how AI systems learn are not separate intellectual projects but deeply connected ones. items.summary: Antarctic polar night brings extreme light deprivation, prolonged isolation and severe circadian disruption, yet longitudinal resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) signatures reflecting neurophysiological alterations in this harsh environment remain poorly characterized. In this exploratory longitudinal research, resting-state EEG recordings with eyes open (EO) and eyes closed (EC) were acquired from 16 Antarctic expeditioners at four mission stages: pre-departure, pre-polar-night, early post-polar-night, and austral summer. items.summary: The Mobile Brain/Body Imaging (MoBI) Conference brings together researchers from various fields using mobile brain imaging from around the world. The 6th International Mobi conference was hosted by the Berlin Brain-Body Imaging Lab at the Technical University of Berlin between August 25-28. items.title: Vector symbolic algebras for the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus
items.summary: The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus for Artificial General Intelligence (ARC-AGI) is a generative, few-shot fluid intelligence benchmark. Although humans effortlessly solve ARC-AGI, it remains extremely difficult for even the most advanced artificial intelligence systems. Inspired by methods for modelling human intelligence spanning neuroscience to psychology, we propose a cognitively inspired ARC-AGI solver. items.title: Brain structure correlates of circulating endocannabinoids and related lipids in early adolescents
items.summary: Abstract The endocannabinoid (eCB) system underlies many biological processes and is thought to be critical in adolescent brain development. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests

items.title: Social Relationships and Mortality Risk: A Meta-analytic Review
items.summary: BACKGROUND: The quality and quantity of individuals' social relationships has been linked not only to mental health but also to both morbidity and mortality. OBJECTIVES: This meta-analytic review was conducted to determine the extent to which social relationships influence risk for mortality, which aspects of social relationships are most highly predictive, and which factors may moderate the risk.
